newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: HORSE RACING-DANOLI BACK TO WINNING WAYS.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-DANOLI BACK TO WINNING WAYS.

text.p: Ireland's latest equine star Danoli returned to winning ways when he triumphed in the grade one Denny Gold Medal Chase at Leopardstown on Thursday.
Danoli was a faller on his last outing at Fairyhouse earlier this month but trainer Tom Foley has spent a lot of time schooling the gelding over fences and his efforts were rewarded.

"I'm delighted," Foley said. "I was always worried he was capable of making a mistake like he did at Fairyhouse so I have to be quite happy with him today. We went out and did our own thing and it all paid off."

Danoli, the 5-2 joint-favourite for the two miles one furlong (3.3-km) race, tracked outsider Crossfarnogue in the early stages but he was driven to the front by jockey Tommy Treacy as the nine runner field turned for home and he stayed clear for an impressive six lengths victory.
Paul Webber's sole British raider, 3-1 chance Land Afar, finished strongly for second place, one length ahead of 20-1 chance Beakstown with joint-favourite Jeffell tiring dramatically on the run-in.
Danoli, a top novice hurdler two seasons ago, will return to Leopardstown for another big chase on February 2.
